extraction.design_notes: Phase 2 clinical trial; hybrid design combining clinical outpatient and human laboratory components; participants, investigators, and outcome assessors were blind to condition; 9 weeks of medication or placebo treatment plus a final assessment visit (week 10)

key_inclusion_criteria: reporting past-year DSM-5 criteria for AUD
past-month endorsement of more than 7 (women) or more than 14 (men) standard drinks in a week with 2 or more heavy drinking episodes (4 or more drinks for women and 5 or more for men)
ability to attend weekly clinic visits and pretreatment and posttreatment laboratory sessions

evidence.quote: Primary inclusion criteria included age 21 to 65 years, reporting past-year DSM-5 criteria for AUD, past-month endorsement of more than 7 (women) or more than 14 (men) standard drinks in a week with 2 or more heavy drinking episodes (4 or more drinks for women and 5 or more for men), and ability to attend weekly clinic visits and pretreatment and posttreatment laboratory sessions.
Of the 48 participants randomized, 34 (71%) were female and 14 (29%) were male. The mean (SD) age was 39.9 (10.6) years.
only the 2 lowest dose sequences (0.25 mg/week for weeks 1-4 and 0.5 mg/week for weeks 5-8) were used prior to primary outcome collection (between weeks 8 and 9)

outcomes.name: estimated volume of alcohol consumed (g-ETOH) during posttreatment laboratory self-administration

evidence.quote: semaglutide reduced posttreatment laboratory consumption with a medium to large effect size for grams of alcohol consumed (β, −0.48; 95% CI, −0.85 to −0.11; P = .01)

outcomes.name: peak breath alcohol concentration (BrAC) during posttreatment laboratory self-administration

evidence.quote: peak breath alcohol concentration (β, −0.46; 95% CI, −0.87 to −0.06; P = .03)
No serious adverse events, adverse interactions with alcohol, or treatment-related discontinuations were recorded.
